steps.prompt: Which character makes you want to keep reading?
steps.a: Jay is a twelve-year-old boy with brown hair. He likes football.
steps.b: Jay would give anything to make the school team, but every time a ball flies at him, he flinches.
steps.reveal: The second Jay wants something (the team) and fears something (the ball). A want and a fear pulling against each other start a story all by themselves.

cards.title: The want
cards.body: Every interesting character wants something: to win, to be noticed, to find a lost dog, to get home. The want gives the story a direction. Readers keep reading to find out whether the character gets it.

cards.title: The fear
cards.body: A fear is what the character is afraid of losing or facing: being laughed at, the dark, letting someone down. When the fear stands in the way of the want, you have a story.

cards.title: Want + fear = story
cards.text: Priya wants to sing at the talent show. Priya is terrified of people staring at her.
cards.note: You already have questions: Will she sing? What will happen on the stage? That pull is what makes readers care.

cards.title: Find the want and the fear
cards.prompt: Tap the word that shows what Omar wants and the word that shows what he fears.
cards.text: Omar saved every coin for the new skateboard, but he dreaded telling his mom how much it cost.

prompts: What does your character want most? Why does it matter to them?
How could their fear get in the way of their want?
